content:
Alice (SRE): Heads-up — I uploaded the postmortem for the ACME Dedicated outage (VPC peering flaps + on-prem route leak). Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1859998881. TL;DR: a peering failover edge-case + a stale on-prem route-policy caused cross-tenant traffic leakage.

dino-bot: New postmortem created: /incidents/1859998881-acme-dedicated-peering-postmortem.md :rotating_light:

Ben (Platform): plz paste the owning action list here, can't open doc from airplane wifi.

Alice (SRE): Action items (short):
1) Harden peering healthcheck + add alerting — owner: Ben (Platform) — due: 2026-06-03
2) Add e2e test for on-prem route-policy detection — owner: Carol (Platform) — due: 2026-06-10
3) Isolation verification script for Dedicated onboarding — owner: Jess (Support) — due: 2026-05-30
4) Customer comms follow-up + runbook update — owner: Ryan (Customer Success) — due: 2026-05-28

Carol (Platform): ack. For #2 I need the customer's firewall/gateway sample logs & config snippets. Alice can you paste the snippets you got?

Alice (SRE): pasted sample below for reference:
```
# sample from customer's gateway
route-map RM-ALLOW permit 10
 match ip address 101
 set ip next-hop 10.0.0.1
!
# observed unexpected route
ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.0.0.254
```

Ben (Platform): For #1 we'll add a dual-check health probe: control-plane state + data-plane TCP handshake across peered AZs. Example probe: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active` + `nc -vz <peer-ip> 5222`. Thoughts?

Carol (Platform): tcp probe sounds good. Probes must run from Dedicated instance netns to avoid false positives. Plan: `peering-health` daemonset on dedicated nodes, container running lightweight tcp probe and route sanity checks.

Jess (Support): I'll own the isolation verification script. Plan: dual-mode script that runs `ip neigh`, `iptables -L -n`, `ip route show`, and a short `tcpdump -nn -c 50 -i eth0 host <customer_ip>` during onboarding. ETA: 5 days.

Ryan (Customer Success): I'll handle comms. Draft ready, sending to legal for approval. Request: can we provide a one-page safe-checklist for the customer's NOC?

Ben (Platform): Also proposing an automated ACL check in our onboarding flow to prevent accepting BGP/routing policies with stale next-hops. Created ticket INF-4821.

Alice (SRE): Note — recurring pattern: this is the 3rd peering-related incident in the last 9 months with asymmetric route installs + slow detection. Proposal: start monthly "isolation retro" to surface recurring config classes. Owner: Alice (SRE). Start date: 2026-06-01.

Carol (Platform): Agree. Also proposing a lightweight linter in onboarding to detect common BGP policy anti-patterns (e.g., default-originate without explicit next-hop validation).

Jess (Support): Quick Q — many customers won't share on-prem BGP logs. Should verification script rely only on passive local checks by default?

Alice (SRE): Good catch. Make script dual-mode: passive-only by default (no customer logs), optional active checks if customer opts-in. Document both modes in the runbook.

Ryan (Customer Success): Legal review might take ~48h. I'll update the postmortem follow-up ticket with final approved language and CC the customer.

Ben (Platform): Assigning INF-4821 to me. I'll open PR for TCP probe today and link it in the ticket.

Carol (Platform): INF-4822 created for the e2e test harness + onboarding linter. Assigned to me.

Alice (SRE): Thanks all. Quick housekeeping: please add PR/issue links to the "Follow-ups" section in the postmortem doc and set due dates in the tracker. I'll run a 2‑week follow-up on 2026-06-10 to verify progress and close loop on owners.

All: :thumbsup:
